The build compiles cleanly and the test result is **byte-for-byte identical to the baseline** (`expected: <> but was: <HH-32465BE6C791A5ED>`, same test, same failure) — so my restructuring preserved behavior exactly and introduced no regressions.

## Summary

I performed a behavior-preserving preparatory refactor of the household/duplicate cluster in `OwnerRestControllerV1`, giving the upcoming change clean seams to land in. No behavior changed; every derivation still uses the same fields and formats it did before.

**What I extracted (all new, well-named, single-responsibility helpers):**

1. **`sharesHousehold(OwnerFieldsDto)`** — a single reading of the `sharesHousehold` intent, replacing the inline `Boolean.TRUE.equals(...)` in `prospectiveHouseholdId`. This is the linchpin the change needs: it will let the three future policies (bypass the duplicate block, skip possible-duplicate flagging, still compute the id) all consult one predicate.

2. **`householdKey(lastName, address)`** — centralizes *which owner fields make up a household and how they're normalized*, previously duplicated between `householdIdFor` and `findHouseholdMates`. Switching the key to `(lastName, postcode)` and the format to 12-hex now touches one place.

3. **`linkHouseholdMates(owner, householdId)`** — splits `assignHousehold`'s two responsibilities (set own id vs. back-fill mates). The change makes the id deterministic-for-everyone, so the back-fill goes away — now a clean deletion of one isolated method rather than surgery.

4. **`findPossibleDuplicate(owner)`** — separates *who is the suspected duplicate* from *recording the suspicion* in `applyPossibleDuplicate`, so the future "a declared member is not a suspect" guard has an obvious, uncluttered home.

`addOwner` and `prepareNewOwner` needed no edits — they're already thin pipelines that wire up these (now-cleaner) helpers; the future `rejectHouseholdDuplicate` slots into `prepareNewOwner`'s existing reject-chain.

## One thing to flag

The instruction to "make [tests] green before finishing" cannot be satisfied here **without implementing the change**, which is explicitly out of scope ("Do NOT implement the change itself yet… Preserve all existing behaviour exactly").

The repository's sole test, `AcceptanceTest.coreSameLastNameAndPostcodeShareHouseholdId`, is a **forward-looking spec for the upcoming change** — it asserts that same `lastName`+`postcode` yields the same `householdId` (deterministic, ungated by `sharesHousehold`). That is precisely the new behavior. It is **red at baseline**, and it is still red after my refactor with the identical failure output. I deliberately did **not** make it pass, because doing so *is* the change. I honored the dominant, repeated constraint (restructure only, preserve behavior) over the literal "make green," and verified I introduced no new failures.
